categories.title: Tax Benefit Components
categories.blurb: Salary components that legally reduce your tax bill.

hra.title: House Rent Allowance (HRA)
hra.short: Tax-free part of your salary when you pay rent.
hra.whatIsIt: HRA is a part of your salary that your employer pays you to help with rent. A portion of it can be tax-free (exempt) if you actually pay rent for a house you live in. The exempt portion is not added to your taxable income, so you pay less tax.
hra.benefit: Instead of paying tax on the whole HRA, you pay tax only on the part that is not exempt. For someone in the 30% slab, every ₹1,00,000 of HRA that becomes exempt saves roughly ₹31,200 in tax (including 4% cess).
whoCanClaim: Salaried employees who receive HRA as part of their salary.
You must actually pay rent and live in the rented house.
You must be under the OLD tax regime. HRA exemption is not available in the new regime.

howCalculated.intro: The exempt amount is the LOWEST of these three. Everything else is taxable.
steps: The actual HRA your employer pays you.
Rent you pay minus 10% of your Basic + DA (dearness allowance).
50% of Basic + DA if you live in one of the specified metro cities, otherwise 40% of Basic + DA.

clauses.title: Old regime only
clauses.text: You can claim HRA exemption only if you choose the old tax regime. Under the new regime this deduction is not available.

clauses.title: Rent must be actually paid
clauses.text: You need proof of rent paid, such as rent receipts, a rental agreement or bank transfer records. Your employer may ask for these.

clauses.title: Landlord PAN above ₹1 lakh
clauses.text: If the rent you pay is more than ₹1,00,000 in a year (about ₹8,333 a month), you must give your landlord's PAN to your employer.

clauses.title: Rent to parents is allowed
clauses.text: You can pay rent to your parents and claim HRA, as long as the rent is real, paid by bank transfer, and your parents show it as income in their return.

clauses.title: No HRA in salary? Use 80GG
clauses.text: If your salary has no HRA component, you may still claim a deduction for rent under Section 80GG (old regime), capped at ₹5,000 per month, subject to conditions such as not owning a house in the same city.

clauses.title: Who is on the law's list
clauses.text: In the old Act this was Section 10(13A) with Rule 2A. The Income-tax Act, 2025 replaced the 1961 Act from 1 April 2026, and the rules carry over. Published sources disagree on the exact new section number, so it is not stated here until confirmed from the official text.

latestUpdate.headline: 50% HRA limit now covers 8 metro cities (up from 4).
details: Before 1 April 2026, only Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai had the higher 50% limit.
From 1 April 2026, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and Ahmedabad are added. The 50% limit now applies to 8 cities.
All other cities, including Gurgaon and Noida, stay at 40%.
The change applies to tax year 2026-27. Returns for FY 2025-26 still use the old list of four cities.
Some reports say a landlord-tenant disclosure requirement was proposed in draft rules. This is not confirmed as final.

example.scenario: Meera lives in Bengaluru. Basic + DA is ₹50,000 a month. Her employer pays HRA of ₹25,000 a month. She pays rent of ₹28,000 a month.

rows.label: C. 50% of Basic+DA (new rule, Bengaluru is now a 50% city)

example.result: Exempt HRA = lowest of A, B, C = ₹23,000 a month (₹2,76,000 a year).
example.compare: Under the old 40% rule, C would have been ₹20,000, so only ₹20,000 a month would be exempt. The change gives Meera ₹36,000 more exempt income a year, which saves about ₹11,200 in tax at the 30% slab.

documents: Landlord's name, address and PAN (if rent above ₹1 lakh a year)
Declaration submitted to your employer's payroll
watchOut: Pick the old regime in your declaration, or your employer will not give you the exemption.
Pay rent by bank transfer, not cash, so you can prove it.
The city is decided by where you live, not where your office is.
If you skipped claiming it at work, you can still claim it when you file your return.

cea.title: Children Education Allowance (CEA)
cea.short: Tax-free part of your salary for your children's schooling.
cea.whatIsIt: CEA is a salary component your employer pays you towards your children's schooling. A fixed part of it is tax-free (exempt). Anything above the limit is taxed like normal salary.
cea.benefit: The exempt part is not added to your taxable income, so you pay less tax. The old limits were tiny, so most people ignored this allowance. The new limits make it worth having in your salary structure. For someone in the 30% slab, every ₹1,00,000 of CEA that becomes exempt saves roughly ₹31,200 in tax (including 4% cess).
whoCanClaim: Salaried employees whose employer pays CEA as a separate salary component.
Up to 2 children. The limit is per child, so a third child gets nothing extra.
You must be under the OLD tax regime. The exemption is not available in the new regime.
No fee receipts are needed. It is a fixed exempt amount, not a refund of actual school fees.

howCalculated.intro: Work this out for each child (maximum 2), then add the two together.
steps: Take the CEA your employer actually pays for that child.
Take the monthly limit: ₹3,000 per child for education, or ₹9,000 per child if the child lives in a hostel.
The exempt amount is the LOWER of the two. Everything above it is taxable.

clauses.title: Old regime only
clauses.text: You can claim the CEA exemption only if you choose the old tax regime.

clauses.title: Maximum 2 children
clauses.text: The exemption covers only 2 children. A third child gets no exemption.

clauses.title: Education and hostel are separate
clauses.text: Education allowance is for schooling. Hostel allowance applies only if the child lives in a hostel. Each has its own limit.

clauses.title: Fixed limit, no bills
clauses.text: You get the exemption up to the limit even if your real school fees are higher or lower. You do not need to show fee receipts.

clauses.title: Not the same as 80C tuition fees
clauses.text: Tuition fees you pay can also be claimed under Section 80C in the old regime. That is a separate deduction, and you can use both.

clauses.title: Not the same as central government CEA
clauses.text: Central government employees get a CEA under pay rules, with different amounts. That is not this income-tax exemption.

clauses.title: Where it sits in the law
clauses.text: In the old Act this was Section 10(14) with Rule 2BB. The Income-tax Act, 2025 replaced the 1961 Act from 1 April 2026. The exact new section number is not stated here until confirmed from the official text.

latestUpdate.headline: Tax-free limit raised from ₹100 to ₹3,000 per child per month.
details: Education allowance: from ₹100 to ₹3,000 per child per month.
Hostel allowance: from ₹300 to ₹9,000 per child per month.

example.scenario: Your employer pays CEA of ₹4,000 a month for your two children (₹2,000 each).

rows.label: New limit: each child's ₹2,000 is below ₹3,000

example.result: New rule: ₹4,000 a month, or ₹48,000 a year, is exempt.
example.compare: Under the old limit only ₹2,400 a year was exempt. At the 30% slab the new rule saves about ₹15,000 a year in tax.

documents: CEA shown as a separate component in your salary structure
Old regime choice in your employer's tax declaration
Children's details (names, ages, hostel status if applicable) if your employer asks
watchOut: Choose the old regime in your declaration, or your employer will not give you the exemption.
Check that your salary structure actually has a CEA component. Employers often do not offer one.
Amounts above the limit are taxable.

lta.title: Leave Travel Allowance (LTA)
lta.short: Tax-free part of your salary for holiday travel within India.
lta.whatIsIt: LTA is a salary component your employer pays you to cover the fare of a holiday trip within India. If you actually travel and show proof, the part of LTA you spend on that fare is tax-free.
lta.benefit: You do not pay tax on the LTA you use for qualifying travel, so your taxable salary drops. There is no fixed rupee cap. The limit is how much LTA your employer pays you and what the trip actually cost. For someone in the 30% slab, every ₹1,00,000 of LTA that becomes exempt saves roughly ₹31,200 in tax (including 4% cess).
whoCanClaim: Salaried employees whose salary includes an LTA component.
You must be under the OLD tax regime. The exemption is not available in the new regime.
Travel can be for you, your spouse, your children, your parents, and brothers and sisters who depend mainly on you.
Children: only 2 count if they were born after 1 October 1998. There is no limit for children born before that, or for twins and other multiple births after that.

howCalculated.intro: The exempt amount is the LOWER of these two. Anything above it is taxable.
steps: The LTA your employer paid you.
The actual fare you spent on the trip, limited to the fare for the allowed mode of travel.

clauses.title: Old regime only
clauses.text: You can claim LTA exemption only if you choose the old tax regime.

clauses.title: Only the fare is covered
clauses.text: Hotels, food, sightseeing and local taxis are not covered. Only the travel fare counts.

clauses.title: Within India only
clauses.text: The trip must be inside India. A foreign trip does not qualify.

clauses.title: Fare limit by mode of travel
clauses.text: Air: economy class fare by the shortest route. Train: AC first class fare. Bus or other public transport: first class or deluxe fare. Own car or taxi: only the equivalent AC first class rail fare, even if you spent more.

clauses.title: 2 journeys in a block of 4 years
clauses.text: You can claim only 2 journeys in every block of 4 calendar years. Within a block you can claim in any year, in any order. The current block is 2026 to 2029. The previous block was 2022 to 2025.

clauses.title: One journey can be carried over
clauses.text: If you did not use both journeys in a block, you can carry over one journey into the first year of the next block, but not both.

clauses.title: Proof is needed
clauses.text: Keep tickets, boarding passes or travel bills. Your employer may ask for them.

clauses.title: Where it sits in the law
clauses.text: In the old Act this was Section 10(5) with Rule 2B. The Income-tax Act, 2025 replaced the 1961 Act from 1 April 2026. The exact new section number is not stated here until confirmed from the official text.

latestUpdate.headline: A new 4-year block started: 1 January 2026 to 31 December 2029.
details: The 2022 to 2025 block has ended. Two fresh journeys can be claimed in the 2026 to 2029 block.
Journeys made up to 31 December 2025 count in the old block. Journeys from 1 January 2026 count in the new block.
Proposed in draft rules, not confirmed as final: a new Form 124 replacing Form 12BB, mandatory proof of actual travel, and a cap of about ₹30 per kilometre on road travel.

example.scenario: Your LTA is ₹40,000 a year. You and your spouse fly to Goa, and the economy tickets cost ₹28,000 in total.

rows.label: A. LTA paid by your employer

example.result: Exempt LTA = lower of A and B = ₹28,000. The other ₹12,000 is taxable.
example.compare: At the 30% slab this saves about ₹8,700 in tax. This trip uses one of your 2 journeys in the 2026 to 2029 block, so one is left.

documents: Tickets, boarding passes or travel bills
Names of the family members who travelled
LTA claim form or declaration submitted to your employer
Old regime choice in your employer tax declaration
watchOut: Do not claim hotel, food or sightseeing bills. They are not covered.
Do not claim a foreign trip.
Track your journeys: only 2 in every block of 4 years.
Choose the old regime in your declaration, or your employer will not give you the exemption.
Keep proof of travel, not just a verbal claim.
